column1: # boru Language Specification: type-system edge cases 3 — generic
# instantiation identity, invariance, bounds; class sealing + the
# nominal Class root
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Companion to generics.tsv / generics-sugar.tsv (schemas) and
# class.tsv (sealed records). Here the EDGES are pinned: instantiation
# identity across spellings and schemas, strict invariance in both
# directions, bound admission per bound kind, loud arity/unbound
# errors, and the sealed-class contract on generic instantiations and
# subclass chains.
# Runs against the production lang registry (test/go/langspec).
# §1  instantiation identity — one node per (schema, canonical args)
def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end (Box of [Integer]) teq (Box of [Integer])
column3: two mentions of one CLASS instantiation are one node

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end (Box of [Integer]) teq (Box of [String])
column3: sibling instantiations are distinct types

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end Box<Integer> teq (Box of [Integer])
column3: the angle sugar and the canonical `of` spelling mint the SAME node

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end Box<Integer> teq Box<Integer>
column3: …and the sugar memoises with itself

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def Cox gen [T] class {v:T} end (Box of [Integer]) teq (Cox of [Integer])
column3: same shape, different schema — identity is per schema, not structural

column1: def Pos (Integer gt 0) def H gen [(T extends Pos)] class {x:T} end (H of [Pos]) teq (H of [(Integer gt 0)])
column3: type arguments CANONICALISE: the named refinement and its interned node instantiate identically

column1: # §2  invariance — Box<Integer> and Box<Number> never mix, either way
def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end def b:(Box of [Integer]) {v:1} b is (Box of [Integer])
column3: an instance is its exact instantiation

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end def b:(Box of [Integer]) {v:1} b is (Box of [Number])
column3: …and NOT the wider one — no covariance

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end def b:(Box of [Number]) {v:1} b is (Box of [Integer])
column3: …and the wider instance is not the narrower one — no contravariance either

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end def b:(Box of [Integer]) {v:1} b is Box
column3: the bare schema name means "any instantiation"

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end 5 is Box
column3: …but still rejects non-members

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def f fn [[x:(Box of [Number])] [Integer] [1]] end f (make (Box of [Integer]) {v:1})
column3: param dispatch is invariant too: a Box<Integer> is refused at a Box<Number> slot

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def f fn [[x:(Box of [Integer])] [Integer] [x dot v]] end f (make (Box of [Integer]) {v:7})
column3: …while the exact instantiation dispatches

column1: # §3  bounds — `extends` checks the type ARGUMENT at instantiation,
#     and the substituted field type checks VALUES at make
def H gen [(T extends Number)] class {x:T} end (make (H of [Float]) {x:1.5}) dot x
column3: a lattice bound admits a subtype argument

column1: def H gen [(T extends Number)] class {x:T} end H of [String]
column3: …and rejects a foreign family loudly

column1: def H gen [(T extends Number)] class {x:T} end H of [Boolean]
column3: Boolean is not a Number — the bound names the violation

column1: def H gen [(T extends Number)] class {x:T} end H of [Never]
column3: Never does not satisfy a lattice bound either

column1: # predicate bound
def H gen [(T extends (Integer gt 0))] class {x:T} end (make (H of [(Integer gt 5)]) {x:7}) dot x
column3: a predicate bound admits a tighter refinement argument

column1: def H gen [(T extends (Integer gt 0))] class {x:T} end H of [String]
column3: …and rejects a foreign family

column1: def H gen [(T extends (Integer gt 0))] class {x:T} end make (H of [(Integer gt 5)]) {x:3}
column3: the SUBSTITUTED field predicate still runs on values at make

column1: # newtype bound
def P (refine Integer) def H gen [(T extends P)] class {x:T} end (make (H of [P]) {x:(make P 1)}) dot x
column3: a newtype bound admits the newtype itself

column1: def P (refine Integer) def H gen [(T extends P)] class {x:T} end H of [String]
column3: …and rejects a foreign family

column1: # generic FN bounds run at dispatch
def f gen [(T extends (Integer gt 0))] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]] f 5
column3: a generic fn's predicate bound admits a satisfying argument

column1: def f gen [(T extends (Integer gt 0))] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]] f 'hi'
column3: …and refuses dispatch on a foreign family

column1: def f gen [(T extends Number)] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]] f 2.5
column3: a lattice bound admits any Number leaf

column1: def f gen [(T extends Number)] fn [[x:T] [T] [x]] f 'hi'
column3: …and refuses a non-Number

column1: # §4  arity — wrong argument counts are loud, and defaults fill
def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end Box of [Integer String]
column3: too many arguments for a class schema

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end Box<Integer, String>
column3: …through the angle sugar too

column1: def Pair gen [K V] class {k:K v:V} end Pair of [Integer]
column3: too few — the error NAMES the unfilled parameter

column1: def R gen [(T default Integer)] class {x:T} end (R of []) teq (R of [Integer])
column3: a default fills a zero-argument instantiation

column1: def R gen [(T default Integer)] class {x:T} end (make (R of []) {x:5}) dot x
column3: …and the defaulted instantiation constructs

column1: # §5  inference — unbound parameters are loud, never silent Any
def Q gen [T] class {} end make Q {}
column3: an empty body gives NO evidence — loud, names the parameter's schema

column1: def Q gen [T U] class {a:T b:U} end (make Q {a:1 b:'x'}) typeof
column3: full evidence infers every parameter

column1: # §6  the sealed-class contract — on plain classes, generic
#     instantiations, and subclass chains alike
# generic instantiations keep the full class contract
def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end make (Box of [Integer]) {w:1}
column3: make rejects an undeclared field on an instantiation

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end make (Box of [Integer]) {v:'no'}
column3: make rejects a wrong-typed field — the SUBSTITUTED type is enforced

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end (make (Box of [Integer]) {v:1}) set v 'x'
column3: set enforces the same substituted type (type_error)

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end (make (Box of [Integer]) {v:1}) set w 2
column3: set on an UNDECLARED field is the distinct sealed_field error

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} end def b (make (Box of [Integer]) {v:1}) b set v 9 end b.v
column3: a conforming write lands

column1: # predicate-typed fields run their predicate at make AND set
def Big (Integer gt 10) def S class {x:Big} (make S {x:50}) dot x
column3: a named-refinement field admits a passing raw value at make (subset semantics)

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def S class {x:Big} make S {x:5}
column3: …and rejects a failing one at make

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def S class {x:Big} def s (make S {x:50}) s set x 5
column3: …and at set

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def S class {x:Big} def s (make S {x:50}) s set x 99 end s.x
column3: …while a passing write lands

column1: # the nominal root: instances live under Class — there is no Object root
def C class {x:1} (make C {}) is Object
column3: the legacy Object root is GONE — the name does not resolve at all

column1: def C class {x:1} (make C {}) is Class
column3: instances root under Class

column1: def C class {x:1} (make C {}) is Map
column3: …and are not Maps, despite the map-shaped schema

column1: def C class {x:1} (make C {}) is Any
column3: …but are members of Any like everything else

column1: # subclass chains — flat fields, nominal widening, sealing end-to-end
def P class {x:1} def P2 refine P {y:2} def P3 refine P2 {z:3} (make P3 {}) is P
column3: a three-level chain widens to the root class

column1: def P class {x:1} def P2 refine P {y:2} def P3 refine P2 {z:3} (make P3 {}) dot x
column3: …and inherits the root default flat

column1: def P class {x:1} def P2 refine P {y:2} def P3 refine P2 {z:3} (make P3 {}) set w 1
column3: sealing covers the whole three-level field set

column1: def P class {x:1} def P2 refine P {y:2} def g fn [[p:P] [Integer] [p.x]] g (make P2 {})
column3: a subclass instance dispatches at a parent-class param

column1: # (dropped) subclass-predicate mismatch dispatch recovery refuses (an open defect the interpreter absorbs); out of corpus for gate purity
# a child cannot redeclare a parent field with a CONFLICTING default/type
def P class {x:1} def P2 refine P {x:5} 1
column3: a different same-name default conflicts with the parent contract

column1: def P class {x:1} def P2 refine P {x:'hi'} 1
column3: …and so does a foreign-family redeclaration

column1: def P class {x:1} def P2 refine P {x:1} (make P2 {}) dot x
column3: an IDENTICAL redeclaration unifies and is allowed

column1: def P class {x:Integer} def P2 refine P {x:1} (make P2 {}) dot x
column3: …as is narrowing a required Integer field to a concrete default

column1: # §7  an ALIAS of an instantiation works in fn signature slots
#     (a plain name where the paren form would not resolve as a type)
def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def BoxI (Box of [Integer]) def mk fn [[] [BoxI] [make BoxI {v:1}]] end (mk) typeof
column3: an aliased instantiation is a first-class return type

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def BoxI (Box of [Integer]) def mk fn [[] [BoxI] [42]] end mk
column2: ERROR:return value 1: expected BoxI, got Integer
column3: …that rejects a raw value

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def BoxI (Box of [Integer]) def BoxS (Box of [String]) def mk fn [[] [BoxI] [make BoxS {v:'s'}]] end mk
column2: ERROR:return value 1: expected BoxI, got BoxS
column3: …and a sibling instantiation, naming both

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def BoxI (Box of [Integer]) def g fn [[b:BoxI] [Integer] [b.v]] end g (make BoxI {v:7})
column3: …and dispatches as a param type

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def BoxI (Box of [Integer]) def BoxS (Box of [String]) def g fn [[b:BoxI] [Integer] [1]] end g (make BoxS {v:'s'})
column3: …rejecting the sibling instantiation at the param

column1: # §8  a NEWTYPE as a type argument — nominal strictness flows through
#     the instantiation into fields and membership
def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def P (refine Integer) end def b:(Box of [P]) {v:(make P 1)} b typeof
column3: a newtype argument names the instantiation

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def P (refine Integer) end (make (Box of [P]) {v:(make P 7)}) dot v
column3: a tagged value constructs the field

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def P (refine Integer) end make (Box of [P]) {v:'x'}
column3: a foreign family is refused at the substituted newtype field

column1: def Box gen [T] class {v:T} def P (refine Integer) end def b (make (Box of [Integer]) {v:1}) b is (Box of [P])
column3:
Box is not Box

— invariance is nominal all the way down
